page_title: How to build a neural network from zero

sources.entry: Build Your Own Neural Net from Scratch in Python

summary.title: How to build a neural network from zero
summary.one_liner: You learn how to write a feedforward neural network in plain Python, with no frameworks, and train it on the MNIST handwritten digit dataset.
takeaways: Load MNIST and preprocess it: reshape so features are rows and examples are columns, and one-hot encode the labels with an identity-matrix indexing trick.
Build a network with ReLU hidden layers and a softmax output for multiclass classification, with biases on hidden nodes.
Add assert statements and guard against division by zero (a small epsilon in the cost) to avoid hard-to-find bugs and overflows.
Instantiate the network with a 2-layer architecture (128 and 32 neurons), train for 200 epochs at learning rate 0.03, then compute accuracy with predict and accuracies methods.
summary.summary: The article walks through implementing a neural network in pure Python without deep learning frameworks. It covers loading the MNIST_784 dataset, preprocessing functions (one-hot encoding and reshaping, with scaling handled inside the network), and activation functions with their derivatives, using ReLU for hidden layers and softmax for the output. The author explains the constructor, cost computation with a small epsilon, predict and accuracy methods, and reports results from training a 128-32 architecture for 200 epochs. Plotting code is omitted but available in the linked GitHub repo.
